properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Non-security uses only: retry-backoff jitter and provider-order shuffling. No key, token or nonce generation uses Math.random — wallet/key generation goes through randomBytes (Node crypto.randomBytes / webcrypto getRandomValues). Recorded as a weak-PRNG presence, not as a keygen weakness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shared default provider API keys shipped as fallbacks: Etherscan defaultToken "919b412a…", QuickNode defaultApiKey "proapi_…", Alchemy "_gg7wSSi0KMBsdKnGVfHDueq6xMB9EkC", Ankr, etc. (src.ts/providers/* and their lib.commonjs/lib.esm/dist copies). Public-by-design — published in the open-source repo and shared by all ethers users, rate-limited by the providers — but they are live hardcoded credentials embedded in every bundle the project ships; rotation rests entirely with the maintainer.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP-39 mnemonic→seed uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with 2048 iterations (mandated by the BIP-39 standard; low vs OWASP's 600k for PBKDF2) in wallet/mnemonic. The legacy Ethereum presale/crowdsale wallet decrypt path (wallet/json-crowdsale.ts:58) uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 2000 iterations and the password itself as salt — a decrypt-only compatibility path for pre-2015 wallet files. Both are real password-based key derivations whose cost parameters are fixed by the formats they must read.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Web3 Secret Storage v3 keystore: encrypt always emits `cipher: "aes-128-ctr"` (json-keystore.ts:304) and decrypt only accepts aes-128-ctr (:75). AES-128-CTR via aes-js is unauthenticated; integrity rests on the keystore's keccak256 MAC field, per the standard format. Changeable only by a keystore format revision, not per-call.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: package-lock.json pins @noble/curves 1.2.0 — the dependency that supplies the secp256k1 implementation. One entry, two names: the lockfile declaration and the code object ALG-673c8f24 are the same asset.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test suites exercising the library's real ECDH feature: SigningKey.computeSharedSecret → secp256k1.getSharedSecret (src.ts/crypto/signing-key.ts:99), the key-agreement operation on secp256k1. Standalone ECDH is harvest-now-decrypt-later material under Shor; PQ replacement would be ML-KEM-768, but the primitive is fixed by the Ethereum/ecosystem tooling this library serves.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 available in the shipped dependency set: @noble/curves 1.2.0 (pinned in package-lock.json) exports ed25519 alongside secp256k1. No application call site — ethers itself uses only the secp256k1 module — but the algorithm ships in the dependency surface the image carries (and remains reachable to any consumer of the same package). Ed25519 is Shor-vulnerable (discrete log on Curve25519); PQ replacement for new designs is ML-DSA / SLH-DSA.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 (secp256r1) available in the shipped dependency set: @noble/curves 1.2.0 (pinned in package-lock.json) exports p256/p384/p521 alongside secp256k1. No application call site — the library uses only secp256k1 for Ethereum operations. Shor-vulnerable curve; availability recorded for CBOM completeness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt is the memory-hard KDF of the Web3 Secret Storage v3 keystore: encryptKeystoreJson defaults to N=131072 (1<<17), r=8, p=1, dkLen=32 with a fresh 32-byte CSPRNG salt (src.ts/wallet/json-keystore.ts:257-260); decryption honors whatever N/r/p/dkLen the keystore file records (json-keystore.ts:250-251). properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: keccak256 — the original Keccak padding (keccak_256 from @noble/hashes/sha3, NOT NIST SHA3-256) — is Ethereum's workhorse hash: address derivation and EIP-55 checksums, transaction and message hashes, EIP-712 typed-data digests, ABI function selectors and event topics, ENS namehash, and the v3-keystore password MAC. All Ethereum identity in this library rests on it. Grover-only (no Shor break); recorded for CBOM completeness — replacement is fixed by the Ethereum protocol. Sampled 10 of 272 site

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 in two roles: (1) BIP-39 mnemonic→seed — PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations, 64-byte output (wallet/mnemonic; standard-mandated, low vs OWASP — flagged under ALG-a861135a); (2) the v3-keystore pbkdf2 KDF path — parameters read from the keystore file (`pbkdf2(password, salt, count, dkLen, algorithm)`, typically c=262144/dkLen=32/prf=hmac-sha256), plus the legacy crowdsale path (2000 iters). Provider: Node crypto pbkdf2Sync on Node, @noble/hashes pbkdf2 in the browser shim. Sampled 10 of 1

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-CTR keystore encryption — the same asset as ALG-e4916d9f (the CTR-mode object): key = first 16 bytes of the scrypt/PBKDF2-derived key, IV from the keystore JSON, via aes-js CTR. Same call chains, described once by the mode and once by the key size.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 in active use: src.ts/crypto/sha2.ts:9 (createHash("sha256") — Node crypto) with the browser twin at src.ts/crypto/crypto-browser.ts:37 (@noble/hashes sha256). Consumers: BIP-39 mnemonic entropy checksum, the SHA256 preimage of BIP-32 fingerprints (see the RIPEMD-160 finding), the crowdsale/keystore PBKDF2 prf, and the exported sha256() API surface. Grover-only, no Shor break.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 declared available via the lockfile-pinned @noble/hashes 1.3.2 (no literal "sha256" string exists in package-lock.json — this is the package→algorithm mapping). Same logical asset as the application's SHA-256 use (ALG-695a1eb5), whose browser path imports @noble/hashes/sha256 at src.ts/crypto/crypto-browser.ts:37 and whose Node path uses Node's createHash("sha256"). Used for BIP-39 mnemonic checksums, BIP-32 fingerprint preimage, crowdsale/keystore KDFs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 available in the shipped dependency set: @noble/hashes 1.3.2 (pinned in package-lock.json) ships a blake3 module alongside the modules ethers does import (sha3/keccak, sha2, ripemd160, scrypt, pbkdf2, hmac). No application call site found; availability recorded because the bundle's dependency surface carries it. BLAKE3 is Grover-only (no Shor break).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA3-256 (the NIST-padding SHA-3) available via @noble/hashes 1.3.2's sha3 module (lockfile declaration). Distinct from what the application actually calls: ethers uses keccak_256 — the original Keccak padding Ethereum standardized before NIST — which is recorded under the SHA-3 use object (ALG-052c24b2). No call site for SHA3-256 itself; availability recorded for CBOM completeness. Grover-only, no Shor break.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-512 digest use: src.ts/crypto/sha2.ts:13 (createHash("sha512") — Node crypto) with the browser twin at src.ts/crypto/crypto-browser.ts:38 (@noble/hashes sha512). Consumers: the exported sha512() API surface and the HMAC-SHA512 compression function inside BIP-32 derivation (filed separately as a finding — the MAC chains at hdwallet.ts:81/320). Grover-only, no Shor break.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes 1.3.2 — the browser-build crypto provider, imported at src.ts/crypto/crypto-browser.ts and lib.esm/crypto/keccak.js: supplies keccak_256 (Ethereum's keccak256, the SHA-3-family hash used for addresses, transaction/message hashes and ABI ids), sha256/sha512, ripemd160, pbkdf2, scrypt and hmac. The image ships these algorithms in dist bundles whether or not the Node path is taken; the Node build reaches the same primitives through Node's crypto module instead.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves 1.2.0 — the elliptic-curve provider, imported at src.ts/crypto/signing-key.ts:7 (and lib.commonjs/crypto/signing-key.js): supplies the secp256k1 implementation used for all Ethereum key operations (ECDSA sign/verify/recover, public-key derivation, ECDH shared secrets). The package also ships ed25519 and P-256/P-384/P-521 (see those lockfile objects) — available in the shipped library even though this application calls only secp256k1.
